question: Parent-side cost of affiliate-staffed sponsors: for the 14 top-50 zero-employee sponsors flagged affiliate_staffed (Fidelity Charitable, GS DAPF, Morgan Stanley GIFT, Ayco, Bessemer, BofA, Raymond James, Renaissance, US Charitable Gift Trust, T. Rowe Price, Dechomai, Greater Horizons, The Signatry, UCLA Foundation), collect the fee basis of each administrative-services agreement from Schedule O, Schedule L/R and audited financial statements on sponsor sites, and estimate parent-borne cost where the 990 shows near-zero opex (BofA 0.15 bps; The Signatry 0.63 bps FY2021)
conclusion_affected: Whether affiliated nationals are cheaper to run or only priced below cost on their own 990; the 0.16x opex ratio for affiliate/zero-staff sponsors
rationale: Affiliated commercial sponsors' opex scales one-for-one with DAF scale (elasticity 1.01, r2 0.92), the signature of asset-based fees to the parent, and at the median top-50 affiliate- or zero-staff national 63% of FY2024 opex is Part IX 11a+11g fees; the 990 records the price paid, not the resource cost

question: Grant-count trend FY2021-2024: collect stated annual grant counts for FY2021-2023 for the 12 sponsors with an FY2024 primary stated count (grant-count-denominators-2026-11-20.csv) from the same giving reports and annual-report chart data, and recompute grants per employee and opex per grant by year
conclusion_affected: Whether grant processing per employee is rising; whether per-grant cost has scale economies
rationale: Only FY2024 grant counts are on file, so grants per employee (Schwab 5,670; JCF 3,891; Vanguard 1,864; NPT 453; FFTC 117) is a cross-section; NPT's chart data already carries FY21-FY25 counts

question: Fee-minus-cost by CF: join cf-daf-fee-census-2026.csv (34+ published schedules) to this file by EIN and compute each CF's effective fee at its own average DAF account against its rule-A and M&G DAF cost per account, FY2024
conclusion_affected: CF pricing below cost at small CFs; the direction-cf-consolidation-fees cost-gap framing
rationale: Band medians suggest published CF fees (median 100 bps at $100k and $1m) exceed rule-A DAF cost at CFs over $1bn (80 bps) but sit below it at $10-100m (149 bps) and under $10m (373 bps); a CF-level join would replace band medians with matched pairs

question: Real-terms trend: deflate FY2021-2024 opex with a published wage or price index (BLS Employment Cost Index for private nonprofit or CPI-U, primary BLS series) to separate wage inflation from efficiency change at community foundations
conclusion_affected: Interpretation of the 21% rise in CF opex per DAF dollar FY2021-24
rationale: Balanced CF panel (n=112): opex +35%, DAF assets +9.4%, accounts +6.4%, employees +14% (median within-sponsor changes, nominal); no deflator is applied, so part of the rise is wages

question: Who staffs the 12 zero-employee sponsors with no affiliate evidence (American Gift Fund, First Midwest Charitable Trust, Cooperative Development Foundation, Oconomowoc Area Foundation and 8 smaller sponsors)? Read Schedule O, Part VII and Schedule R of their latest 990s and classify as volunteer-run, affiliate-staffed or contracted
conclusion_affected: Staffing-model flag; per-employee and per-account efficiency of zero-employee sponsors
rationale: American Gift Fund reports $3.86m of FY2024 opex, zero employees and no 11a/11g fees, so neither the employee nor the fee route explains who does the work

question: Extend the four-year panel to the full DAFRC universe: extract FY2021 returns for the roughly 1,300 sponsors not in this sample (sponsor-cost-structure.csv covers FY2022-2025 only) and rerun the by-type regressions with sponsor fixed effects (within-sponsor scale elasticity)
rationale: Cross-sectional elasticities mix scale with sponsor type and mission; a within-sponsor estimate needs more years per sponsor and a larger panel than the 112-CF balanced panel here
